name: TIMOR-LESTE

flag.title: Timor-Leste Flag
flag.note: Red, yellow & black triangles, white star

lead: Timor-Leste only became independent in 2002, making it one of the world's newest nations. Tucked onto a tropical island between Indonesia and Australia, it has emerald mountains, coral beaches, and fish-packed seas. Fewer tourists visit here than almost anywhere in Asia — so its reefs and rainforests stay gloriously wild.

facts.sub: Coastal city on the north shore

geo: Timor-Leste covers the eastern tip of Timor island, ringed by the Timor Sea and the Banda Sea. Rugged mountains spine the whole country — perfect for cool-weather coffee farms. The enclave of Oecusse sits separately, wrapped by Indonesian territory.

The Coral Triangle laps its shores, making these some of the most biodiverse waters anywhere. Ataúro island, about 30 km north of Dili, has been called the world's most fish-rich island by marine scientists.
animals: The Timor deer — called rusa — roams mountain forests and is a national symbol. Coconut crabs, the world's largest land crab, haul themselves up palms on Ataúro island. Dugongs (sea cows) graze seagrass beds in the Timor Sea.

Sperm whales and dolphins surf deep channels just offshore — whale-watching boats leave from Dili. The forests shelter the Timor imperial pigeon, a plump grey bird found only on Timor and nearby Wetar island.
culture: Timorese life revolves around the uma lulik — the sacred house, a thatched ancestral home every family tends with offerings and ceremonies. Woven cloth called tais carries clan stories in its patterns; no two designs are alike.
The tebe-tebe is a circle dance where whole villages lock arms and sing together for hours. Coffee is the nation's soul crop — chemical-free mountain beans are prized by specialty roasters worldwide.
history: Portugal colonised Timor from the 1500s, trading in sandalwood and coffee. Japan occupied it in World War II; after the war Portugal returned, but in 1975 Indonesia invaded and ruled harshly for 24 years, causing enormous loss of life.

A 1999 UN referendum saw 78% vote for independence despite widespread violence. In 2002 Timor-Leste became Asia's newest nation. Nobel winners Bishop Belo and José Ramos-Horta led the international fight for freedom.
wows: Timor-Leste is the only country in Asia that uses the US dollar as its everyday currency.
Ataúro island holds a world record — over 250 reef fish species counted per survey site on average.
The country has more than 30 distinct indigenous languages, roughly one for every valley.
Timorese mountain coffee is organic and fair-trade certified, sold in speciality shops across the US.
Tatamailau means 'Grandfather of All' — local belief says ancestral spirits travel to its summit.
Sperm whales pass so close to Dili that local spotters hear them blowing in the still of the night.
Timor-Leste was the 21st century's very first new country, gaining full independence on 20 May 2002.

myths.fact: It is fully independent since 2002. Indonesia governs West Timor on the same island, but Timor-Leste has its own government, flag, currency, and UN seat.

myths.myth: "There's nothing to see or do there"
myths.fact: Divers rate its reefs among the world's top five for fish diversity, and whale-watching, hiking, and weaving tours all run year-round from Dili.
